title: आत्मसमीक्षाबाट पुनर्जागरणको खोजी : एमाले राष्ट्रिय भेलाले देखाएको नयाँ दिशा
content:
The real strength of a political party is not determined solely by its leaders, positions, election results, or access to power. The real strength of a party lies in its ideas, principles, organizational life, relationships with the people, the ethics of its leadership, and the confidence of its cadres. When a party reaches a difficult political situation, its true character, leadership ability, and organizational maturity are tested. At that time, the CPN (UML) was at a crucial political juncture. The political situation after the Genji Rebellion, the challenges created by the election results, the disappointment seen among the people, the psychological pressure within the party, and the slowness in organizational activities have shown the party the need for serious introspection. In this backdrop, the national gathering to be held on Mangsir 2 and 3 should not be just a formal meeting or a program to review past decisions. It should be a historic opportunity to establish the party's political direction, leadership style, organizational restructuring, and relations with the people on a new basis. The Central Committee, Central Bodies, Provincial Office bearers, District Office bearers and Municipal Chairmen and Vice Chairmen who will participate in this gathering are important responsible levels of the political and organizational functioning of the party. Therefore, their participation should not be limited to mere representation. They should take the responsibility of making a realistic analysis of the current situation of the party, assessing their responsibilities and determining the future course of action. The political message conveyed by the lizard story The famous short story 'The Lizard' by the great Russian storyteller Anton Chekhov has effectively exposed the fear of human opportunistic character power and the double standards of justice. The main character of the story, police inspector Ochumelov, is walking in the market square when he encounters a man bitten by a dog. At first, he talks about taking the dog under control and punishing the owner. But when he hears that the dog belongs to the general, his speech and behavior change. He starts blaming the victim. After some time, suspicions are raised again that the dog does not belong to the general. Then his decision changes again. As the information that the dog belongs to the owner changes, the police inspector's speech, behavior, and decision also change repeatedly. This story is not just a character portrayal of a police inspector. It is a symbol of the tendency of power and authority to change truth, justice, and conscience. A similar tendency can be seen in politics as well. The tendency to support thought leadership or decisions when they are favorable to oneself and oppose them when the situation is unfavorable is opportunism. The mentality of praising when close to a powerful person, criticizing when weak, failing to show one's abilities when given responsibility but blaming others for failures is also a political form of the lizard tendency. In the current situation of the CPN (UML), this story raises a serious question - do we make decisions based on truth, principles, organization, and the needs of the people, or on the basis of individuals, positions, power, and factional influence? The National Assembly should be able to give a clear answer to this. Disagreements within the party are natural. Criticizing the leadership is also a healthy practice in party life. But criticism and opposition should be based on truth, facts, and the party's interests. A political culture of making decisions based on what is right rather than who is on whose side should be established. Leadership loyalty is not blind support for individuals, but commitment to the party's principles, ideas, methods, and the interests of the people. 1. From the psychology of defeat and despair to confidence The Genji Rebellion and subsequent political developments have exposed the expectations, discontent, and desire for change of a new generation in Nepali politics. The election results have also forced traditional political parties to rethink their working style and relationship with the people. In such a situation, it is not unusual for the leaders and cadres of the CPN (UML) to show disappointment. But disappointment should not be used as a basis for inaction. There are some significant problems within the party right now. Organizational activity is slower than before. Decreased commitment to responsibility among leaders and workers. Internal conflicts and misunderstandings cannot be resolved. Weakening organizational unity through factional thinking and personal interests. Increasing tendency to blame others for failures rather than reviewing one's own responsibilities. The mentality of avoiding one's own weaknesses by blaming only the national political situation is evident. These problems cannot be solved by simply giving instructions. For that, the leadership must begin introspection within itself. How much work was done on the responsibility you received yesterday? How active was your committee? How much did you reach out to the people? How many new members were added? How many opportunities were given to the youth? How much were the party's ideas and policies established in society? Every responsible leader must be able to answer these questions for themselves. The first foundation of renaissance is the culture of acknowledging one's own weaknesses and paving the way for improvement, rather than evading one's responsibilities by pointing out the weaknesses of others. 2. Upcoming Tasks: Party Renaissance on Eight Basis A clear course of action and a measurable action plan should be set at the CPN (UML) national convention to re-establish the party at the center of people's trust. For this, an analysis of the basis or concepts presented as future tasks at the convention is also necessary, and this is positive, but due to shortcomings in implementation, there has always been some confusion as decisions have not been made as planned. For this, the following eight issues can be taken forward as the party's future political and organizational tasks. a) True: Up to the public level The first foundation of politics is truth. The real picture of the problems faced by the people, the achievements and weaknesses of the party, and the national situation must be conveyed to the people. It is necessary to promote only the achievements in one's favor and to respond based on facts. The party should conduct a truth-based dialogue campaign at the grassroots level. b) Party: Up to the basic class and community The real base of the party is farmers, laborers, low and middle-income families, the landless, entrepreneurs, businessmen, employees, teachers, students, youth, women, and various social communities. The party should be directly involved in their happiness, sorrow, employment, education, health, inflation, agriculture, entrepreneurship, and social security. People's trust cannot be gained by holding meetings at the party office alone. We must reach out to people's doorsteps. We must listen to their problems and take initiatives to solve them. c) Organization: From planning to measurement The activism of an organization is more important than its size. A committee should be evaluated based on how much work it is doing rather than how big it is. Each committee should have clear standards for annual work plans, quarterly reviews, membership expansion, training, public relations, and social activities. After the responsibility is given, there should be monitoring. Those who do the work should be encouraged, and those who do not fulfill the responsibility should be re-evaluated as necessary. The success of the organization should be measured by the results, not the number of meetings. d) Youth and women: From party responsibilities to leadership development Representation of youth and women cannot be ensured simply by involving them in party programs. They must be given real opportunities in policy-making, organizational operations, decision-making processes, and leadership responsibilities. The technological creativity, energy, and desire for change of the new generation must be combined with the political experience, struggle, and ideological maturity of the older generation. An environment must be created to develop the new generation into leadership while respecting the contributions and experiences of the older leaders. Generational change in leadership is not an insult to the older generation, but a combination of experience and new energy. e) Renaissance: Civil rights and livelihoods The party's renaissance should be seen in the lives of the people, not in slogans. Civil rights, freedom of expression, good governance, corruption control, employment, education, health, social justice, and economic opportunity should be made the party's main agenda. The people should be able to perceive the party as a protector of their rights and a force that struggles for the improvement of people's livelihoods. f) Opposition: Up to civil rights and livelihoods Being in opposition is not a state of political inaction. It is an opportunity to raise the voice of the people, hold the government accountable, and present alternative policies. We must be able to support the good works of the government and factually oppose its wrong works. Both tendencies of opposing every issue or supporting every issue are not the character of a responsible opposition. We must play an effective role in parliament, on the streets and at the grassroots level in matters related to the protection of civil rights, good governance, economic development and people's livelihood. g) Digital Resistance: Until Truth Prevails Today's political competition is not limited to traditional assemblies and organizations. Social media and digital media have played a major role in shaping public opinion. Misinformation, confusion, rumors, and unfounded accusations can influence the political environment, but digital protest does not mean cursing, making personal accusations, or suppressing dissenting views. The party's ideas, policies, and achievements should be conveyed to the public based on facts, evidence, logic, and ideological clarity. A digital culture of admitting mistakes and refuting false propaganda with evidence should be developed. H. Continuous struggle: Towards the destination of prosperous Nepal, happy Nepalis Political struggle should not be just for position and power. Its ultimate goal should be to improve the living standards of the people and national prosperity. To translate the national aspiration of a prosperous Nepal, happy Nepalis into reality, emphasis should be placed on increasing production, creating employment, industrialization, agricultural modernization, developing education and health infrastructure, and building a self-reliant economy. The party should link its political struggle with the positive changes seen in the daily lives of the people. 3. Leadership Responsibilities: Self-Review and Necessary Reorganization The leadership must be able to take responsibility for the success or failure of any political party. Leadership is not just about holding office, it is about making decisions in difficult situations, uniting the organization, boosting the morale of the cadres, and maintaining the trust of the people. In the current situation, responsible party leaders need to answer three questions. First - How much work was done on the responsibility you received? Second - How active and result-oriented was the committee under your leadership? Third - What changes should we make to improve the party in the coming days? Without answering these questions, an organization cannot become strong by blaming others. There should be organizational restructuring as needed. However, the basis of restructuring should not be factions, close personal relationships, professional relationships, or temporary political equations. It should be based on efficiency, contribution, honesty, ideology, clarity, public relations, and results. The contributions, struggles, and experiences of older leaders in the party are invaluable assets. Their experience should not be ignored. Similarly, the energy, new thinking, technological knowledge, and desire for change of the new generation should not be stopped. Only by respecting experience and incorporating new energy can competent, dynamic, and forward-looking leadership be built. 4. The national assembly should not only make decisions, but also commit to implementation. We have made many political decisions, proposals and commitments in the past. But the question of how much of those decisions have been implemented is equally important. This gathering must clearly acknowledge both the achievements and the shortcomings in reviewing past decisions. In particular, concrete decisions are needed on the following issues. Identify the actual situation of all levels of party committees and carry out organizational restructuring. Determine the work, responsibilities, and performance standards of each responsible official. Resolve internal conflicts, misunderstandings, and factional problems through methods, dialogue, and impartial decisions. To activate inactive organizations and make necessary changes in places that are unable to fulfill their responsibilities. Ensure meaningful participation of youth, women, and the new generation in decision-making processes and leadership. Identifying the problems of the people and conducting public relations and public service programs from the local to the national level Institutionalize digital communication, ideological training, and fact-based public relations. Arrange for regular monitoring, evaluation and accountability at every level. A work order should be given with a time frame, responsible person, and measurable achievements for the implementation of the plan prepared by the national assembly. 5. The party can be made the center of people's trust again. The CPN (UML) is a party with a long history of struggle, organization building and government operation in Nepal's political history. It has played an important role at various times in the fields of democratic movements, social justice, infrastructure development, nationality and economic and social transformation. But past contributions alone do not ensure future political success. Society is changing. The aspirations of the new generation have changed. Citizens are looking to political parties for accountability, transparency, good governance, and results. Therefore, the party should not think that it is free from current weaknesses by discussing its historical contributions. What is needed today is the courage to introspect, the honesty to admit mistakes, the will to improve, and the commitment to implement. There should be a debate of ideas within the party, but there should not be division of the organization for personal interests. There should be respect for the leadership, but leadership should not be above the question. Criticism should not be considered hostility and disagreement should not be dismissed as factionalism. Party unity does not mean everyone praising the same person, but rather uniting on the basis of methods and principles to achieve the same objective. Conclusion: May the national gathering be the beginning of introspection, renaissance, and new resolve. The leaders and cadres who participated in the national gathering on November 2/3 should be able to return with a clear message. Now, we will not wait for someone else to do something to change the situation of the party, but we will start the change ourselves. We will not cover up the weaknesses of yesterday, but move forward by accepting them. We will not shy away from our responsibilities, but by taking responsibility. Be guided by the party's ideas, principles and national interests, not by factional interests. Prioritize the strengthening of the organization over the protection of positions. Party leadership should be free from the tendency to change decisions according to circumstances and power, like police inspector Ochumelo in Anton Chakhava's story 'Lizard'. The criteria for truth and justice should not be individuals, positions and power, but principles, methods and facts. The leadership the party needs today is not one that seeks praise, but one that takes responsibility. The party needs cadres who are not just critical of others, but who reach out and work among the people. The party needs an organization. If the experience of the older generation, the energy of the new generation, the leadership potential of women, the creativity of the youth, and the activism of ordinary cadres can be integrated, the party can build new political trust. The national assembly should not create an environment where people return with just expressing disappointment, but rather with new hope, a clear course of action, and a determination to implement. Because the renaissance of a political party does not come from the decisions of a single assembly alone. It is proven by the behavior of the leadership, the activism of the workers, the working style of the organization, and the results experienced by the people. The question now is not only who will lead the party, but what the leadership will do for the party and the people. The question now is not whose faction is stronger, but who will build an organization that will win the trust of the people. The question now is not only who did what in the past, but who is capable of taking and will take responsibility for the future today. May the national gathering of the CPN (UML) become a historic starting point for self-reflection, organizational renaissance, leadership accountability, and re-establishment of public trust, with the goal of fulfilling the national aspiration of a prosperous Nepal, happy Nepalis. May this national gathering transform the frustration within the party into hope, inaction into activism, factional mentality into unity, and defensive psychology into creative political initiatives. Best wishes. Thank you!

Leadership loyalty is not blind support for individuals, but commitment to the party's principles, ideas, methods, and the interests of the people.

1. From the psychology of defeat and despair to confidence

The Genji Rebellion and subsequent political developments have exposed the expectations, discontent, and desire for change of a new generation in Nepali politics. The election results have also forced traditional political parties to rethink their working style and relationship with the people.

In such a situation, it is not unusual for the leaders and cadres of the CPN (UML) to show disappointment. But disappointment should not be used as a basis for inaction.

There are some significant problems within the party right now.

These problems cannot be solved by simply giving instructions. For that, the leadership must begin introspection within itself. How much work was done on the responsibility you received yesterday? How active was your committee? How much did you reach out to the people? How many new members were added? How many opportunities were given to the youth? How much were the party's ideas and policies established in society? Every responsible leader must be able to answer these questions for themselves.

The first foundation of renaissance is the culture of acknowledging one's own weaknesses and paving the way for improvement, rather than evading one's responsibilities by pointing out the weaknesses of others.

2. Upcoming Tasks: Party Renaissance on Eight Basis

A clear course of action and a measurable action plan should be set at the CPN (UML) national convention to re-establish the party at the center of people's trust. For this, an analysis of the basis or concepts presented as future tasks at the convention is also necessary, and this is positive, but due to shortcomings in implementation, there has always been some confusion as decisions have not been made as planned. For this, the following eight issues can be taken forward as the party's future political and organizational tasks.

a) True: Up to the public level

The first foundation of politics is truth. The real picture of the problems faced by the people, the achievements and weaknesses of the party, and the national situation must be conveyed to the people. It is necessary to promote only the achievements in one's favor and to respond based on facts.

The party should conduct a truth-based dialogue campaign at the grassroots level.

b) Party: Up to the basic class and community

The real base of the party is farmers, laborers, low and middle-income families, the landless, entrepreneurs, businessmen, employees, teachers, students, youth, women, and various social communities.

The party should be directly involved in their happiness, sorrow, employment, education, health, inflation, agriculture, entrepreneurship, and social security. People's trust cannot be gained by holding meetings at the party office alone. We must reach out to people's doorsteps. We must listen to their problems and take initiatives to solve them.

c) Organization: From planning to measurement

The activism of an organization is more important than its size. A committee should be evaluated based on how much work it is doing rather than how big it is. Each committee should have clear standards for annual work plans, quarterly reviews, membership expansion, training, public relations, and social activities.

After the responsibility is given, there should be monitoring. Those who do the work should be encouraged, and those who do not fulfill the responsibility should be re-evaluated as necessary. The success of the organization should be measured by the results, not the number of meetings.

d) Youth and women: From party responsibilities to leadership development

Representation of youth and women cannot be ensured simply by involving them in party programs. They must be given real opportunities in policy-making, organizational operations, decision-making processes, and leadership responsibilities.

The technological creativity, energy, and desire for change of the new generation must be combined with the political experience, struggle, and ideological maturity of the older generation. An environment must be created to develop the new generation into leadership while respecting the contributions and experiences of the older leaders. Generational change in leadership is not an insult to the older generation, but a combination of experience and new energy.

e) Renaissance: Civil rights and livelihoods

The party's renaissance should be seen in the lives of the people, not in slogans. Civil rights, freedom of expression, good governance, corruption control, employment, education, health, social justice, and economic opportunity should be made the party's main agenda. The people should be able to perceive the party as a protector of their rights and a force that struggles for the improvement of people's livelihoods.

f) Opposition: Up to civil rights and livelihoods

Being in opposition is not a state of political inaction. It is an opportunity to raise the voice of the people, hold the government accountable, and present alternative policies.

We must be able to support the good works of the government and factually oppose its wrong works. Both tendencies of opposing every issue or supporting every issue are not the character of a responsible opposition. We must play an effective role in parliament, on the streets and at the grassroots level in matters related to the protection of civil rights, good governance, economic development and people's livelihood.

g) Digital Resistance: Until Truth Prevails Today's political competition is not limited to traditional assemblies and organizations. Social media and digital media have played a major role in shaping public opinion.

Misinformation, confusion, rumors, and unfounded accusations can influence the political environment, but digital protest does not mean cursing, making personal accusations, or suppressing dissenting views.

The party's ideas, policies, and achievements should be conveyed to the public based on facts, evidence, logic, and ideological clarity. A digital culture of admitting mistakes and refuting false propaganda with evidence should be developed.

H. Continuous struggle: Towards the destination of prosperous Nepal, happy Nepalis

Political struggle should not be just for position and power. Its ultimate goal should be to improve the living standards of the people and national prosperity.

To translate the national aspiration of a prosperous Nepal, happy Nepalis into reality, emphasis should be placed on increasing production, creating employment, industrialization, agricultural modernization, developing education and health infrastructure, and building a self-reliant economy. The party should link its political struggle with the positive changes seen in the daily lives of the people.

3. Leadership Responsibilities: Self-Review and Necessary Reorganization

The leadership must be able to take responsibility for the success or failure of any political party. Leadership is not just about holding office, it is about making decisions in difficult situations, uniting the organization, boosting the morale of the cadres, and maintaining the trust of the people.

In the current situation, responsible party leaders need to answer three questions.

Without answering these questions, an organization cannot become strong by blaming others. There should be organizational restructuring as needed. However, the basis of restructuring should not be factions, close personal relationships, professional relationships, or temporary political equations. It should be based on efficiency, contribution, honesty, ideology, clarity, public relations, and results.

The contributions, struggles, and experiences of older leaders in the party are invaluable assets. Their experience should not be ignored. Similarly, the energy, new thinking, technological knowledge, and desire for change of the new generation should not be stopped. Only by respecting experience and incorporating new energy can competent, dynamic, and forward-looking leadership be built.

4. The national assembly should not only make decisions, but also commit to implementation.

We have made many political decisions, proposals and commitments in the past. But the question of how much of those decisions have been implemented is equally important. This gathering must clearly acknowledge both the achievements and the shortcomings in reviewing past decisions.

In particular, concrete decisions are needed on the following issues.

A work order should be given with a time frame, responsible person, and measurable achievements for the implementation of the plan prepared by the national assembly.

5. The party can be made the center of people's trust again.

The CPN (UML) is a party with a long history of struggle, organization building and government operation in Nepal's political history. It has played an important role at various times in the fields of democratic movements, social justice, infrastructure development, nationality and economic and social transformation.

But past contributions alone do not ensure future political success. Society is changing. The aspirations of the new generation have changed. Citizens are looking to political parties for accountability, transparency, good governance, and results.

Therefore, the party should not think that it is free from current weaknesses by discussing its historical contributions. What is needed today is the courage to introspect, the honesty to admit mistakes, the will to improve, and the commitment to implement. There should be a debate of ideas within the party, but there should not be division of the organization for personal interests. There should be respect for the leadership, but leadership should not be above the question. Criticism should not be considered hostility and disagreement should not be dismissed as factionalism.

Party unity does not mean everyone praising the same person, but rather uniting on the basis of methods and principles to achieve the same objective.

Conclusion: May the national gathering be the beginning of introspection, renaissance, and new resolve.

The leaders and cadres who participated in the national gathering on November 2/3 should be able to return with a clear message. Now, we will not wait for someone else to do something to change the situation of the party, but we will start the change ourselves. We will not cover up the weaknesses of yesterday, but move forward by accepting them. We will not shy away from our responsibilities, but by taking responsibility.

Be guided by the party's ideas, principles and national interests, not by factional interests. Prioritize the strengthening of the organization over the protection of positions. Party leadership should be free from the tendency to change decisions according to circumstances and power, like police inspector Ochumelo in Anton Chakhava's story 'Lizard'. The criteria for truth and justice should not be individuals, positions and power, but principles, methods and facts.

The leadership the party needs today is not one that seeks praise, but one that takes responsibility. The party needs cadres who are not just critical of others, but who reach out and work among the people. The party needs an organization. If the experience of the older generation, the energy of the new generation, the leadership potential of women, the creativity of the youth, and the activism of ordinary cadres can be integrated, the party can build new political trust.

The national assembly should not create an environment where people return with just expressing disappointment, but rather with new hope, a clear course of action, and a determination to implement. Because the renaissance of a political party does not come from the decisions of a single assembly alone. It is proven by the behavior of the leadership, the activism of the workers, the working style of the organization, and the results experienced by the people.

The question now is not only who will lead the party, but what the leadership will do for the party and the people. The question now is not whose faction is stronger, but who will build an organization that will win the trust of the people. The question now is not only who did what in the past, but who is capable of taking and will take responsibility for the future today. May the national gathering of the CPN (UML) become a historic starting point for self-reflection, organizational renaissance, leadership accountability, and re-establishment of public trust, with the goal of fulfilling the national aspiration of a prosperous Nepal, happy Nepalis.

May this national gathering transform the frustration within the party into hope, inaction into activism, factional mentality into unity, and defensive psychology into creative political initiatives. Best wishes. Thank you!
